claim_being_audited: That the current release can be certified now because current aggregate readiness evidence is sufficient, with the grant compliance regression handled by disclosure-based governance rather than stale prior approval or informal monitoring.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation before launch.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes are contextual only and cannot substitute for current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness evidence supports launch readiness in part, but does not eliminate the need to satisfy the disclosure or mitigation requirement for the subgroup regression.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release documentation or model-card text showing explicit disclosure of the grant compliance regression and current evaluation results.
Provide approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation documentation if the team intends to certify without disclosure-based cure.
Provide evidence that the grant compliance weakness is not material to the named launch use case, if that is the intended argument.
specific_concerns: The policy predicate for certification is not fully satisfied by the admissible record because there is no evidence that current release documentation or model-card materials were actually updated to disclose the grant compliance weakness.
The grant compliance slice is below the warning threshold for a named launch use case, which is evidence of a material segment weakness requiring disclosure or approved mitigation before launch.
The release thread contains only an informal monitoring comment; the record lacks reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or approved risk acceptance.
Prior approval is explicitly stale relative to the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot carry the certification decision.
unsupported_claims: The implied claim that certification is presently compliant, rather than only conditionally supportable after disclosure is completed.
Any claim that informal post-launch monitoring is sufficient governance coverage for the current subgroup regression.
Any claim that prior approval meaningfully substitutes for current-release documentation or reviewed risk acceptance.
